headline: Gold and silver hit their lowest in over a year, while India plants far less wheat after a dry monsoon.
summary: Gold and silver fell to their lowest prices in more than a year. Traders expect the Fed (the US central bank) to keep raising interest rates. In India, farmers are planting much less wheat after the weakest monsoon in over a decade, and rice is getting pricier across Asia. Oil is far below October's $125 average, and the US, China and Russia promised more fuel.
lookback: The last read said a December rate rise looked nearly certain. Fed officials kept sounding tough, and gold kept falling, to its lowest in about 14 months. More ships were hit near Iran, as the last read warned. But oil barely moved, because the US has plenty in storage. Two watch items are still ahead: the OPEC+ meeting and FAO's November food prices. We couldn't open Malaysia's palm oil board this time, so there is no new palm oil storage number.

items.title: Gold and silver sink to their lowest in over a year
items.text: Gold fell to about $3,780 an ounce on Wednesday, The Hindu BusinessLine reported. Silver fell to about $46. Both are at their lowest in more than a year. Traders think the Fed (the US central bank) will raise interest rates faster than expected. That lifts the dollar, and gold pays no interest, so it looks less attractive. Both metals peaked on 29 January, gold near $5,600 and silver near $122. So silver has lost almost two thirds since then. Gold averaged $4,105 in October and silver $57. The live price on this page slid further on Thursday.

items.title: India plants far less wheat, and rice gets pricier
items.text: India is the world's second-biggest wheat grower. Its farmers are set to cut wheat planting by the most in 26 years, Reuters reported. The monsoon (the summer rainy season) was the weakest in over a decade. With dry fields, many farmers are switching to other crops. That could mean less wheat and higher food prices in India. El Niño (the Pacific running warm) brings another risk: a hot February and March could hurt the crop. Thai rice also hit its highest price in nearly two years. World rice and wheat prices were both 37% higher in October than a year before.

items.title: Oil stays far below October, and three leaders promise more fuel
items.text: Brent crude (the main world oil price) was about $92 a barrel on Friday. October's average was $125. The leaders of the US, China and Russia met in China on Thursday. They said they plan to make and supply more fuel, like gasoline and diesel. Experts doubt it will add much fuel. The Strait of Hormuz (the narrow sea lane by Iran) is still far quieter than before the war. If oil stays this low, gas prices could ease in the coming months.

items.title: Russia sells less wheat abroad, but the world grows more
items.text: The IGC (the world grain council) cut its guess for Russia's wheat sales abroad again, Interfax reported. It's the fourth cut in four months, to about 38.5 million tonnes. But the IGC raised its guess for the world's wheat harvest. Russia and Ukraine also have unusually large amounts in storage. So the world isn't short of wheat for now. Wheat in October was 9% below its recent high.
